mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000,000 units signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 1000000 for the current month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in economic output, which typically precedes negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 1% month-over-month coincident with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher wage growth and consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate earnings downgrades and recession fears.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a simultaneous monetary tightening and inflationary pressure episode, which typically results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-month avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12-month avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 5% for four consecutive months signals a robust residential investment recovery, which historically coincides with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to construction sector and related equity outperformance.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > 5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 55% of triggered episodes.
